comments.body:
Issue branch at:

https://github.com/fcrepo/fcrepo/tree/fcrepo-1061

ConfigA tests now run successfully in a "Cargo-ized" Tomcat. Proceeding to try with Jetty, then will move on to other test configs. I will be using Maven profiles to try and parcel out the various permutations of container and application config.

Maven profiles now available:

configA
configB
tomcat7x
jetty8x

A combination of config and container is required to make a test run.

This branch now successfully tests configA and configB in Tomcat, via:

mvn clean verify -P tomcat7x,configA
mvn clean verify -P tomcat7x,configB

Jetty is still failing about five or ten tests.
It's now not clear at this point that Jetty ever passed the test suite with any of the configs. I'm going to leave it be and concentrate on getting the other configs passing in Tomcat.
I'm stopping work on this for the nonce as we head towards 3.6. When I take it back up, the next step will be to update the actual test code to match the new CXF-based dependencies.

I'm wondering if http://jira.codehaus.org/browse/CARGO-574 blocks our ability to use Cargo to replace our integration tests as they're currently written. I don't really remember the details of our tests that assume SSL but I seem to recall tests that assume the availability of both HTTP and HTTPS connectors.

See: https://github.com/mediashelf/fedora-client

for a certain kind of example.
